newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Carter hopes U.S. raids on Iraq are over.
newsitem.headline: Carter hopes U.S. raids on Iraq are over.

text.p: Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter said on Thursday he hoped his country's missile attacks against Iraq were over but added they had been a tempered response to Saddam Hussein's abuse of the Kurds.
Carter told reporters the Iraqi leader should bow to international demands.
"I hope the raids are over and that Saddam Hussein will comply with United Nations resolutions," he said after meeting Austrian President Thomas Klestil in Vienna's Hofburg palace.
"And I hope that the Arab countries, who have not supported the raids, understand that this is a limited response to the abuse of the Kurds," he said.

Most Arab countries criticised or condemned the U.S. operation. Saudi Arabia, Washington's chief strategic ally in the Middle East, maintained official silence. Only Kuwait, liberated from Iraqi occupation by a U.S.-led military coalition in the 1991 Gulf War, openly supported the attacks.

On Tuesday and Wednesday, the United States fired a hail of missiles on air defence targets in southern Iraq to minimise Iraqi resistance to its warplanes policing an expanded no-fly zone, which now nearly reaches the capital Baghdad.
The attacks came in retaliation for Saddam's recent incursion into the Kurdish-controlled areas in northern Iraq.
The United States said it believed there were credible reports that Iraqi forces killed 100 Kurds last weekend.

Carter, a former Democratic Party president defeated by Republican Ronald Reagan in 1980, brokered the 1979 peace deal between Israel and Egypt, the first peace treaty forged between the Jewish state and an Arab country.
